author: Mike Helms
text:
You are probably experiencing what is called compression lows.
Where have you placed the sensor? What is happening is, while you sleep, you are pressing hard on the sensor which causes low readings.

With me, it was a little trial and error, learning where to put my sensor on my arm to avoid these lows. I am a side sleeper

author: Peggy Stasik
text: Yes  my provider said that the lows can happen if there is pressure on the CGM like when sleeping on side or I like to tuck my arm under same causes pressure. Also she recommended doing as you are with your finger stick as well, I use the note option to document my finger sticks. Otherwise the CGM seems to normalize and I no longer get those low in the 50's any more  plus I turned off all the alarms I could access.
